propositions: Compaction non-atomically leaves tracker working tree dirty with untracked regenerable artifacts (SNAPSHOT.json, *.retired, .archived deletions) when the detached sweep process is interrupted before commit.

The next reconverge union-merge fails with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge' when origin has pushed the same compaction artifacts, causing permanent wedge because abort-only handler and untracked-blind push-recovery cannot clear those files.
Local ticket events including critical attestations are stranded off origin when the store wedges, unreachable until manual recovery involving git checkout and untracked cleanup.

Moving named untracked collision paths to git-common-dir quarantine before retry allows the merge to succeed and both parents to be kept, preserving all local commits while adopting origin's authoritative versions.
Genuine content conflicts and merge failures unrelated to untracked overwrites must still abort and preserve local state with fsck-recover hint, maintaining today's abort-only fallback behavior.
Untracked files not explicitly named by git (including .tmp-event-* and real event appends) are never quarantined or touched, ensuring uncommitted work is never lost.
